clue.text: One is the first churchman with less feeling

parts.note: a cardinal is a prince of the Church, ranking first after the Pope
numb means without feeling, so number (more numb) means having less feeling

explanation.surface: A claim that a senior cleric is the most emotionally deadened of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is the comparative of numb, said 'nummer'. 'is the' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the first of the counting numbers, the cardinals, as opposed to the ordinal first.

clue.text: Maybe representative of sons, green crops supplied

indicators.note: made supple, so the letters of the three words are worked loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's sons provided with fresh vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied' is read as 'made supple', loosening SONS GREEN CROPS into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US House of Representatives is one example of a member of Congress, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Representative toy for gadabout during revolution

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as one event happens during another

parts.note: a roll is a turning over, a revolution
read as 'gad about': the letters of gad stirred about to give AGD

explanation.surface: A doll bought for a restless traveller in a time of political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria splits the single word 'gadabout' as gad plus 'about', the second half acting as the anagram signal on the first; 'during' is the container signal and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a cloth toy shaped to represent a person.

clue.text: Never willing, as it were, to take little road from highway

indicators.note: to take a piece from a word is to remove it, and 'from' names the word it leaves

parts.note: an interstate is a US highway
R is a short abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Advice to leave a minor road when joining a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take ... from' removes R from INTERSTATE. The definition is jokey: someone intestate died without making a will, so they were 'never willing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without a will, punningly 'never willing'.

clue.text: Energy in a lover a panacea?

indicators.note: the energy symbol goes inside the word lover

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Asks whether a romantic partner full of energy is a cure for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes into LOVER after the O to make LOEVER, flanked by the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera gel is promoted as a cure-all remedy, and the question mark admits it may not truly be one.

clue.text: Old relative — sister? Not quite clear

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its tail is cut short

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Puzzling over whether a family member is really a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last two letters of CLEAR to leave CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuncle is an archaic form of uncle, used by the Fool in King Lear.

clue.text: Holding note is low Welsh girl

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: low in the sense of base or mean
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl singing a held low note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Megan is a common Welsh girl's name, a pet form of Margaret.

clue.text: English language about love and happiness

indicators.note: the word for a language goes around the letter for love

parts.note: Latin is a language
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: English as a language that speaks of love and joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: All but one doubtfully sane artist's mother at New England college

indicators.note: something doubtful is uncertain, so the letters are put in doubtful order

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
RA (Royal Academician) is an artist, plus the 's
a dam is an animal's mother
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in New England

explanation.surface: Describes an artist's mother at a US college as barely sane.
explanation.walkthrough: SANE rearranged gives ASNE; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As near as dammit is an idiom meaning almost, all but.

clue.text: Covering near where people live around Gateshead

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: the town goes around the letter

parts.note: a town is a place where people live
read as 'Gate's head', the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: Describes something in the area around the Tyneside town of Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, but here it is split as 'Gate's head', the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a garment that covers the body in bed.

clue.text: Provenance of pot found by ordinary people

definitions.meaning: pot is cannabis, also called ..., so its origin is where it grows from
the ordinary members of a party or movement, the rank and file

explanation.surface: Asks where cannabis comes from and finds the answer among the common folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Roots of the weed are the origin of the plant, and the phrase also means the rank and file.

clue.text: See 10
Shakespearean promoter of love first transferred into plant

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed into the plant

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
A as in A1 or grade A, first class
lent means handed over for a time

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character who furthers romance is moved first into a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Valentine is Orsino's attendant who carries his master's suit to Olivia.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine in Twelfth Night acts as a go-between for Orsino's love.

clue.text: Cross about article depicting model village

indicators.note: the cross goes about the article

parts.note: a saltire is a diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An angry painting of an ideal village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicting' is a link. Saltaire is a Victorian model village near Bradford, built by Titus Salt for his mill workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltaire is a planned workers' village in Yorkshire, a famous example of a model settlement.

clue.text: Star pupil's marked surrounds

definitions.meaning: a black eye, a bruise around the pupil of the eye

explanation.surface: Praises a top schoolchild whose work is graded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild but is the centre of the eye; the bruised area around it is a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiner is slang for a black eye and also means someone who shines.

clue.text: Stuck in the mud? Don't let anyone see you jump!

parts.note: to hide is to keep out of sight
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Advice to someone leaping out of a muddy hole to do it in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' is a link; read as an order, 'hide, bound!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-in-the-mud is narrowly conventional and set in old ways, which is what hidebound means.

clue.text: The bottom line is about where you pay — prison

indicators.note: the base goes about the till

parts.note: a base is the bottom line of a figure
a till is where you pay in a shop

explanation.surface: A remark that money is what really matters, behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bottom line' looks like a business idiom but is the base of a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress prison stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Assigner of sergeant's part may be sternutatory

parts.note: the role of Sgt Pepper, from the Beatles album
a caster assigns parts in a play

explanation.surface: Someone casting the Beatles' famous sergeant might make you sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. 'Sternutatory' means causing sneezing, which is what a shaker of ground spice may do.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for ground pepper can make people sneeze, so it may be described as sternutatory.

clue.text: Large bill here for a nut, about one pound

indicators.note: the nut goes about the other pieces

parts.note: a pecan is a nut
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asks the price of a nut, about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like money, but is the bird's beak; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is famous for its huge bill, so a large bill is found here.

clue.text: Shakespearean promoter of love: I leave Persian king to God

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: I leaves the king's name, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: Darius was a king of Persia

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's matchmaker says he will hand a Persian king over to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. Pandarus is the go-between in Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandarus brings Troilus and Cressida together, giving English the word pander.

clue.text: Length of program on little pig and two setters?

parts.note: a runt is the smallest pig of a litter
a setter calls himself I or me, giving two pronouns for the setter
a setter calls himself I or me, giving two pronouns for the setter

explanation.surface: A computer program about a small pig and a pair of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' are not dogs but crossword setters, who refer to themselves as I and me; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Run time is how long a program or film lasts.

clue.text: See 17
Not wanting to be involved in cattle run

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drover who does not want to join a cattle drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant means unwilling, not wanting to do something.

clue.text: Petrol makes load?

parts.note: read as a split phrase: fuel makes the motor go, and together the words name a load carried

explanation.surface: Asks whether fuel creates a freight burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the load carried by a ship, plane or vehicle.

clue.text: Lowest taxed property in Hastings?

definitions.meaning: the lowest council tax band for a UK home
the surname of Hastings ..., first president of Malawi

explanation.surface: A cheap house in the Sussex seaside town of Hastings.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings is a Sussex town, but here it is Hastings Banda's first name. UK council tax puts homes in bands, Band A the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Band A is the cheapest council tax band, and Banda is the surname that follows Hastings.

clue.text: Take place — the Guardian's — without minimal space

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: in the Guardian, the paper's own is ours, OUR
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a tiny volume

explanation.surface: A newspaper event happening without room to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or take place.

clue.text: Element to — at length — turn into what's nearly a great victory

indicators.note: the pieces go into the shortened victory
nearly the whole word, so its last letters are cut

parts.note: a triumph is a great victory
an ell is an old measure of length
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: Something elementary that at last turns into almost a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts PH from TRIUMPH to leave TRIUM; 'to', 'at' and 'what's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellurium is a chemical element, symbol Te.

clue.text: If that's really the hat you want, I'm not stopping you

definitions.text: If that's really the hat you want, I'm not stopping you

parts.words: If that's really the hat you want, I'm not stopping you
parts.note: a stock phrase disclaiming responsibility, taken literally of a hat worn on the head

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the consequences are your responsibility, which fits someone choosing a dubious hat.
